chunks: Al-Bazanti narrated from ʿAbd al-Karim ibn ʿAmr, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ziyad, from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said:

It is not proper for a man to divorce his wife and then take her back while he has no desire for remaining with her, and then divorce her again. This is the harmful treatment that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden, except when he divorces and then takes her back while intending to keep her.

key_terms.الضِّرَارُ: harmful conduct intended to injure another party
key_terms.الْإِمْسَاكَ: retaining and keeping the wife in marriage
key_terms.يُرَاجِعَهَا: to take her back during the revocable period

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to divorce a wife, take her back, and then divorce her again without intending to keep her?
ai.summary: This hadith forbids a man from using divorce and revocation as a means of harming his wife without a genuine intention to continue the marriage. It teaches that returning to one’s wife after divorce is only proper when there is sincere intent to retain and maintain the marital bond.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4762 - Al-Bazanti narrated from ʿAbd al-Karim ibn ʿAmr, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"It is not appropriate for a man to divorce his wife and then reconcile with her when he has no need or intention for her, only to divorce her again. This is the harm (ḍirar) that Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden. However, if he divorces her and then reconciles with her with the sincere intention of keeping her, then it is permissible."
